target.title: fix(ui): avoid splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs in session display peer-id tail
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the sidebar display name for an unnamed direct-message session could emit isolated UTF-16 surrogate halves when the peer id contains astral characters (e.g., emoji).

## Why This Change Was Made

`shortenPeerId` sliced the tail of the identifier with raw `String.prototype.slice(-6)`, which can bisect surrogate pairs. It now uses the repository's existing `sliceUtf16Safe` helper so the shortened tail always falls on a valid UTF-16 boundary.

## User Impact

Session labels in the Control UI sidebar remain well-formed when peer identifiers contain non-BMP characters.

## Evidence

- Replaced `trimmed.slice(-6)` with `sliceUtf16Safe(trimmed, -6)` in `ui/src/lib/session-display.ts`.
- Added a regression test in `ui/src/lib/session-display.test.ts` covering an astral character at the tail boundary.
- Focused tests pass: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/session-display.test.ts`.
- Lint clean: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ui/src/lib/session-display.ts ui/src/lib/session-display.test.ts`.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Before the patch, a peer id like `"12345😀67890"` would have produced a tail containing an isolated surrogate half. After the patch it returns `"…67890"`.
- **Real environment tested:** Local checkout of `fix/session-display-peer-id-utf16` at `8996aa6b8a`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { resolveSessionDisplayName } from "./ui/src/lib/session-display.ts"; const samples = ["agent:main:telegram:direct:491234567890", "agent:main:telegram:direct:12345😀67890"]; for (const k of samples) { const n = resolveSessionDisplayName(k); try { encodeURIComponent(n); console.log("ok"); } catch(e){ console.log("FAIL", e); } console.log(JSON.stringify(n)); }'
  ```
  And to verify the display names survive a real disk write/read round-trip:
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { resolveSessionDisplayName } from "./ui/src/lib/session-display.ts"; import { writeFileSync, readFileSync, mkdtempSync } from "node:fs"; import { tmpdir } from "node:os"; import { join } from "node:path"; const f = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "sd-")), "names.txt"); const samples = ["agent:main:telegram:direct:491234567890", "agent:main:telegram:direct:12345😀67890"]; const names = samples.map(resolveSessionDisplayName); writeFileSync(f, names.join("\n"), "utf8"); const r = readFileSync(f, "utf8"); console.log(r); console.log("round-trip ok:", r === names.join("\n"));'
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```
  ok
  "Telegram · …567890"
  ok
  "Telegram · …67890"

  Telegram · …567890
  Telegram · …67890
  round-trip ok: true
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The regression test `does not split UTF-16 surrogate pairs when shortening peer ids` passes, `encodeURIComponent` succeeds on every display name, and the names survive a disk write/read round-trip.
- **What was not tested:** No live Control UI sidebar render; change is a pure string-formatting helper.

_AI-assisted PR: changes and tests were generated with AI assistance and manually reviewed._

target.title: fix(agents): keep subagent run ID mask from splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the subagent run-ID mask used in lifecycle log/error metadata could emit isolated UTF-16 surrogate halves when the run ID contains astral characters (e.g., emoji).

## Why This Change Was Made

`maskRunId` sliced its prefix/suffix with raw `String.prototype.slice`, which can bisect surrogate pairs. It now uses the repository's existing `sliceUtf16Safe` helper so the masked ID always falls on valid UTF-16 boundaries. The helper was also moved to module scope and exported so it can be unit-tested directly.

## User Impact

Subagent lifecycle warnings and error metadata remain well-formed when run IDs contain non-BMP characters.

## Evidence

- Moved `maskRunId` to module scope in `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts` and exported it.
- Added regression tests in `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts` covering ASCII masking and astral boundary cases.
- Existing lifecycle controller tests continue to pass.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Before the patch, a run ID like `"abc😀xxxxxxxxx"` produced `"abc\ud83d…\ude00xxxx"` (isolated surrogate halves). After the patch it returns `"abc…xxxx"`.
- **Real environment tested:** Local checkout of `fix/mask-runid-utf16` at `71f75fbfa526d0041851c3530662325cc35ac424`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { maskRunId } from "./src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts"; for (const v of ["run-1234567890", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(10), "x".repeat(10) + "😀abc", "a😀b", "short"]) console.log(JSON.stringify(maskRunId(v)));'
  ```
  And to verify the masked values survive a real disk round-trip without corrupting:
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { maskRunId } from "./src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts"; import { writeFileSync, readFileSync, mkdtempSync } from "node:fs"; import { tmpdir } from "node:os"; import { join } from "node:path"; const f = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "mr-")), "m.txt"); const samples = ["run-1234567890", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(10), "x".repeat(10) + "😀abc", "a😀b"]; const masked = samples.map(maskRunId); writeFileSync(f, masked.join("\n"), "utf8"); const r = readFileSync(f, "utf8"); console.log(r); console.log("round-trip ok:", r === masked.join("\n"));'
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```
  "run-…7890"
  "abc…xxxx"
  "xxxx…abc"
  "***"

  run-…7890
  abc…xxxx
  xxxx…abc
  ***
  round-trip ok: true
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The regression test `does not split UTF-16 surrogate pairs at mask boundaries` passes, `encodeURIComponent` succeeds on every masked value, no isolated surrogates are emitted, and the joined masked values survive a disk write/read round-trip.
- **What was not tested:** No live subagent lifecycle failure path; change is a pure string-formatting helper.

_AI-assisted PR: changes and tests were generated with AI assistance and manually reviewed._
